Title: Diagnosis  
Details:  
The test `testEscapedQuote_LANG_477` uses a pattern with escaped single quotes: `"it''s a {0,lower} 'test'!"`. The test fails likely due to an OutOfMemoryError reported when using `ExtendedMessageFormat` with a custom format registry and single quotes in the pattern.

Reviewing the `ExtendedMessageFormat` constructor reveals it stores the registry and applies the pattern with `applyPattern(pattern)`.

Examining `applyPattern` shows it parses the pattern char by char, treating single quotes (`QUOTE`) by calling `appendQuotedString`. This method handles escaped quotes by checking for escaped quote sequences (`''`) and appending them properly.

The problem stems from how `applyPattern` parses quoted strings. If the pattern contains single quotes, it relies on `appendQuotedString` to skip over quoted segments safely without infinite loops or excessive memory use. However, the current mechanism may fail to properly handle nested or escaped quotes when combined with a custom format registry. The cycle of parsing repeated escaped quotes can cause the parser to get stuck or accumulate an unbounded amount of string data, leading to OutOfMemoryError.

The critical part is that in `applyPattern`, the case for `QUOTE` calls `appendQuotedString` to append quoted segments and move the parsing position. If this does not advance correctly (due to a bug or incorrect escaping handling), the loop over the pattern will never progress, repeatedly processing the same characters and causing memory overflow.

Recent bug reports do not indicate related parsing issues, so the root cause is limited to the logic of quoted string handling in `ExtendedMessageFormat` when combined with custom registries.

This explains why the test pattern with double single quotes causes OutOfMemoryError with custom format registries: the parsing of quoted portions loops without end or accumulates huge strings due to improper advancing of parse position or wrong handling of escaped quotes.

Fix should focus on ensuring `appendQuotedString` and the parsing loop properly handle escaped sequences to prevent infinite loops or memory blow-ups.

---

Which methods to fix:  
`ExtendedMessageFormat.applyPattern(java.lang.String)`  
`ExtendedMessageFormat.appendQuotedString(java.lang.String,java.text.ParsePosition,java.lang.StringBuffer,boolean)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
